sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

content.text:
Make a website that, if everyone saw and used it, would improve the world for the greatest number of people.

Build this as an interactive web page in the current directory.
- The entry point is index.html. Put your code in JavaScript ES modules loaded from it
  (`<script type="module" src="main.js">`), and add a short README.md.
- You may use npm packages: `npm install <package>` here, then import them by name
  (`import * as THREE from "three"`). No CDN URLs and no import maps.
- Afterwards the page is packaged into one self-contained index.html with esbuild: every script and
  stylesheet index.html references is bundled with everything it imports. Load assets the page needs
  with `import` (they become data URLs) or generate them in code, never by URL string.
- The packaged page runs offline in a sandboxed iframe: no network requests, and no localStorage,
  cookies or other storage (they throw there).
- Check that it packages: `esbuild main.js --bundle --format=esm --outfile=/dev/null` must succeed.
  Don't build or package the page yourself; that happens afterwards.
- To look at the page yourself, serve it locally and screenshot it in headless Chrome (Chrome is
  installed, and a driver such as puppeteer-core or playwright can be npm-installed here). Save every
  screenshot you look at as a .jpg file, never .png: each image you read stays in your context, and a
  long session of large .png files can hit the provider's per-request image limit and end the run.
- Only create or edit files inside the current directory.
- Finish with a short summary of what you built.

content.text: The core experience will have three practical layers: a guided “conversation untangler,” a one-minute breathing reset, and a field guide for replacing common accusatory phrases. Everything will run locally in the page, with no accounts, tracking, or saved personal text.

arguments.content:
Skip to the conversation tool
COMMON
GROUND
The practice Take a pause Field guide
Start a repair ↗

A practice for being human

Less reacting.
More understanding.

A private space to untangle what you’re feeling, understand what you need, and find words that bring you closer—not further apart.

Untangle a conversation → ▶ I need a minute first
  • ✓ Nothing is saved
  • ✓ No sign-up
  • ✓ Always free
✳ ✳
THE TWO-MINUTE SHIFT
“
You never listen to me. You obviously don’t care about what I have to say.

A judgment, a generalization, and a guess about their intentions.

YT

Same hurt. Different doorway.

You don’t have to be calm to begin.
You only have to be willing to pause.

SCROLL TO CONNECT

A small but radical idea

Most conflicts aren’t about
who’s right.

They’re about something that matters, asking to be heard. Four small shifts help us hear it.

  1. 01

    Start with the moment

    Describe what a camera could capture. No motives, labels, or “always” and “never.”

    Observation, not evaluation
  2. 02

    Name your inner weather

    “Hurt” opens a door that “you don’t care” closes. Feelings are information, not indictments.

    Feelings, not accusations
  3. 03

    Find what matters

    Under frustration is often a need for respect, rest, clarity, trust, or connection.

    Needs, not blame
  4. 04

    Make a doable ask

    Invite one specific, positive action. A real request leaves room for the other person to say no.

    Requests, not demands

Inspired by the principles of Nonviolent Communication. Made for ordinary, imperfect humans.

Your turn

Turn a reaction into
a conversation.

Think of one real moment. We’ll take it apart gently, then put it into words you can actually say.

This stays with you. Your words never leave this page.
THE CONVERSATION UNTANGLER Step 1 of 4
What happened?

Stick to what a camera would have caught. Just this one moment, without interpreting it.

Try an example:
Tip: begin with “When…” or “During…”0 / 360
How did it land?

Choose up to three honest feelings. Not what they did wrong—what happened inside you.

There are no wrong answers here.

↳

A useful distinction: “I feel ignored” points at their behavior. “I feel lonely” or “I feel frustrated” names your experience.

What mattered to you?

Under every difficult feeling is something you value. Choose one or two needs.

Needs are universal. Strategies are how we meet them.

↳

You’re not being needy. Naming a need makes the conversation about something both people can understand.

What could you ask for?

Make it specific, positive, and doable now. A request is an invitation, not a test.

Try “Could we…” or “Would you be willing to…”0 / 280

YOUR WORDS, PUT TOGETHER LIVE

A message you can stand behind.

When the moment you describe,

I felt your feeling

because I needed what matters to you.

Would you be willing to one clear next step?

Say it in your own voice. You don’t need to use every line.

Before the words

Give your nervous system
a way out.

You don’t have to solve everything while your body is sounding an alarm. Take one minute to make a little room between what happened and what you do next.

  • 01Breathe in gently through your nose.
  • 02Let the exhale be a little longer.
  • 03Return when you feel 1% more choice.
A 60-SECOND RESET1:00
Ready?just as you are

No need to take a deep breath.
Just let it be easy.

Keep this in your pocket

Words that open doors.

A few translations for the moments when your first draft is more likely to start a fight than finish one.

THE FIRST DRAFT
“You never listen to me.”
Closed with a conclusion
instead
THE DOORWAY
“I want to understand each other. Could we each take two minutes to speak without interrupting?”
Open with a shared purpose

Kindness doesn’t mean avoiding the hard thing.
It means making it possible to hear.

Try it with your words ↑
✳

A world with more common ground

One conversation
won’t fix everything.
It can change what happens next.

Begin with yours →
COMMON
GROUND

Made for the space between people.

A self-guided reflection tool, not a substitute for professional support.
If you’re in immediate danger, prioritize safety and contact local emergency support.

↑

arguments.content:
# Common Ground

A private, offline-friendly web page for turning difficult reactions into clearer, kinder conversations. It combines:

- A four-step **Conversation Untangler** based on observations, feelings, needs, and requests.
- A live, copyable message draft with gentle prompts for blame or vague language.
- A guided **60-second breathing reset**.
- An accessible, keyboard-friendly **field guide** for common conflict situations.

## Run locally

Serve this directory with any static server, for example:

```sh
python3 -m http.server 8000
```

Then open `http://localhost:8000`.

No account, analytics, network calls, or browser storage are used. Personal text exists only in the current page and disappears on refresh. This is a self-guided reflection tool, not professional or emergency support.

## Structure

- `index.html` — semantic page structure
- `styles.css` — responsive visual design and reduced-motion support
- `main.js` — entry point
- `practice.js` — guided message builder
- `breathing.js` — breathing timer
- `ui.js` — examples, tabs, and reveal interactions

## Packaging check

```sh
esbuild main.js --bundle --format=esm --outfile=/dev/null
```

- Four-step conversation builder: observation → feelings → needs → request
- Live, copyable message draft with gentle blame-language prompts
- Guided 60-second breathing reset
- Interactive field guide for common conflicts
- Responsive, accessible design with reduced-motion support
- No accounts, tracking, network requests, or browser storage
